canonical_name: Admission (cell shortlist before the token is chosen)
plain_what: Before the model picks a word, it narrows the 4,096 candidates to those stored in a few 'drawers' (cells) near where its read points. A word in a drawer that was not opened can never be chosen. So the number of correct words that make it into the opened drawers sets a ceiling on everything the read can achieve.
how_it_works: The writer takes the read's integer vector q (B blocks of 8 numbers, B = 4 registered) and picks a token in two steps, never scoring all 4,096 words. Admission: every token sits in a product cell given by the pair (orbit root of its first block, orbit root of its last block), so 16 x 16 = 256 cells. The K nearest occupied cells to q are admitted, where distance is the L1 distance of q's first block to the cell's first root plus the same for the last block, ties by cell number. K is 8 in the lineage of record and at most 16. Ranking: among tokens in admitted cells the nearest by total L1 over all blocks wins; ties go to the lowest token id. A target outside the admitted cells cannot be predicted whatever the read does, so target-admitted rows cap top-1 and top-8. Training uses a hinge: 8 x token margin + width x address margin (objective A, nearest rival cell) or + width x rank penalty (objective R: how many occupied cells outrank the target beyond K). Codebook moves change a token's cell, so learning can eject targets from the shortlist. The admission-preserving rule audits a fixed TRAIN anchor panel every 64 batches and rejects any interval that shrinks admission.
geometry: Product of orbit-root labels of one 16-root E8 orbit on the first and last 8-D block gives 256 cells; L1 distance on integer root coordinates. Codebook initialisers: xorshift seed (16 distinct vectors), PrimeZeta (prime-rank indexing with complex-plane zeta phases, 4,096 distinct vectors), and address-structured placement near each token's predecessors' cells.

rule_compat.D11: Integer only: compare, absolute difference, add; the hinge weights 8 and width are applied by shift-and-add (checked_scaled_add), no multiplier. No D11 served export of an admission artifact has been measured in the audited records.
rule_compat.D23: Compliant: a hard top-K by integer distance and a hinge over declared rivals; no softmax, no exponential, no normalised output head.
rule_compat.D30: Compliant: no matmul; token_distance is a sum of absolute differences.
rule_compat.D32_D37: D32 integer, GPU-only, counterfactual moves; codebook table moves are VectorBlock parameters. Host code only counts and compares stored outputs (D24). D37 float training of admission has not been proposed.

open_questions: Why does learning move target tokens out of the cells that predecessor placement chose, and how fast?
Does the guard's 24-row margin reject too much (RULE_EFFECTIVELY_NOOP) or too little?
Is 256 cells too coarse; would a finer address (more blocks) lift admission without raising K?
At what point does a 16-token-per-cell injective codebook make ranking, not admission, the bottleneck?
Can a hinge reward admission without letting the model collapse tokens onto a few cells?
